- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast increase after spike to 3–5% max.
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% from next forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days of true values show strong upward trend, reduce forecast peak by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.67, +0.67), model often misaligns with sentiment; adjust forecast to match sentiment direction only if sentiment is >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.
- Avoid forecasting >10% above recent 7-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish and confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
